skill_drafts.name: LLM Framework Integration Setup
skill_drafts.description: Establish and configure AgentOps monitoring for a chosen LLM framework (OpenAI, LangChain, LiteLLM, Gemini, etc.). Selects the appropriate integration module, initializes the client, and validates connection.
contraindications: Framework already initialized and monitoring active
Only adding a single micro-operation to existing setup
Debugging existing agent behavior without re-initialization
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Select target LLM framework', 'detail': 'Choose from CrewAI, Gemini, Google ADK, LangChain, LiteLLM, OpenAI, OpenAI Agents, SmolAgents, Watsonx, or xAI'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Locate integration module', 'detail': 'Access the corresponding framework directory in the AgentOps repository'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Initialize AgentOps client', 'detail': 'Create and configure the client with framework-specific parameters'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Validate connection', 'detail': 'Verify that monitoring is active and client is ready for agent execution'}
triggers: Starting a new agent project with a specific LLM framework
Need to enable AgentOps monitoring before agent execution
constraints: Target framework must be one of: CrewAI, Gemini, Google ADK, LangChain, LiteLLM, OpenAI, OpenAI Agents, SmolAgents, Watsonx, xAI
AgentOps client library must be available
Framework-specific credentials or API keys must be configured
cautions: Ensure framework selection is finalized before initialization
Validate API credentials before attempting connection
Monitor initialization logs for connection errors
output_contract: AgentOps client initialized and connected to the chosen framework; monitoring active for subsequent agent calls; ready for agent execution

metadata.prompt: Select the target LLM framework from available integrations. Locate the corresponding integration module directory. Initialize the AgentOps client with framework-specific configuration. Validate that the client is connected and monitoring is active before proceeding with agent execution.

skill_drafts.name: Multi-Tool Agent Orchestration
skill_drafts.description: Coordinate multiple tools or agents in a single execution flow, managing tool selection, parameter passing, and result aggregation. Handles complex tool chains and multi-agent system coordination.
skill_drafts.objective: Execute coordinated multi-tool or multi-agent workflows
contraindications: Simple linear tool call without selection logic
No tool interdependencies or coordination required
workflow_steps: Identify all tools or agents required for the workflow
Validate tool parameters and input compatibility
Execute tools in correct sequence or parallel batches
Pass outputs from upstream tools as inputs to downstream tools
triggers: Agent requires multiple tools in sequence or parallel
Complex tool chains with interdependencies detected
constraints: All tool dependencies must be resolved before execution
Tool parameters must be validated before passing to next stage
Result aggregation must preserve execution order and metadata
cautions: Monitor for circular dependencies in tool chains
Ensure timeout handling for long-running tool sequences
output_contract: All tools executed in correct order; results aggregated and returned to caller; tool dependencies resolved; execution metadata preserved

metadata.prompt: Execute a coordinated workflow across multiple tools or agents. Determine tool execution order based on dependencies, pass outputs from one tool as inputs to the next, aggregate final results, and handle tool selection logic. Ensure all interdependencies are resolved before returning aggregated results to the caller.

skill_drafts.name: Asynchronous vs. Synchronous API Call Selection
skill_drafts.description: Choose and execute the appropriate calling pattern (async or sync) for LLM API calls based on workload, concurrency requirements, and framework support. Handles both patterns transparently.
skill_drafts.objective: Select and execute correct async/sync API call pattern
workflow_steps: Detect framework type and its async/sync support
Select pattern: async if multiple concurrent calls needed and supported, else sync
Execute API call using selected pattern
triggers: Need to optimize for latency or throughput
Framework supports both async and sync patterns
constraints: Framework must support the selected pattern
Caller must handle async context if async pattern selected
Response must be returned without blocking or concurrency errors
cautions: Async pattern requires proper event loop management
Sync pattern may block other operations in concurrent environments
Pattern mismatch with framework can cause runtime errors
output_contract: API call executed with correct pattern; response received and returned; no blocking or concurrency errors

metadata.prompt: Evaluate the calling context: determine if multiple concurrent API calls are needed, check framework support for both async and sync patterns, and select the pattern that optimizes for latency or throughput. Execute the selected pattern and return the response without blocking or concurrency errors.

skill_drafts.name: Agent Design Pattern Reference
skill_drafts.description: Catalog of reusable agent design patterns including customer service automation, job workflow automation, markdown validation, and text-to-SQL conversion. Provides templates and best practices for common agent use cases across multiple frameworks.
skill_drafts.objective: Reference and select appropriate agent design pattern for a given use case
contraindications: Pattern already selected and implementation underway
Designing a novel or experimental agent architecture
No design guidance needed; implementation-only phase
triggers: Designing a new agent from scratch
Need to understand common agent patterns and best practices
Looking for a template or example for a specific use case
constraints: Reference asset; does not execute workflows directly
Patterns are templates; adaptation to specific requirements is caller responsibility
Examples assume familiarity with underlying frameworks (LangChain, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents, etc.)
output_contract: Caller receives pattern description, applicable use cases, example code reference, and guidance on when to apply the pattern. Caller is responsible for selecting and adapting the pattern to their specific requirements.

metadata.prompt: When designing a new agent, consult this reference to identify applicable patterns. Review the pattern description, examine the provided example code, and adapt the template to your use case. Patterns cover single-agent and multi-agent scenarios.
